arxiv-2112-12529.title: Mott-Hubbard Insulating State for the Layered van der Waals FePX 3 (X:S, Se) As Revealed by NEXAFS and Resonant Photoelectron Spectroscopy
arxiv-2112-12529.creator: Yichen Jin, Mouhui Yan, Tomislav Kremer, Elena Voloshina, Yuriy Dedkov
arxiv-2112-12529.description: Abstract A broad family of the nowadays studied low-dimensional systems, including 2D materials, demonstrate many fascinating properties, which however depend on the atomic composition as well as on the system dimensionality. Therefore, the studies of the electronic correlation effects in the new 2D materials is of paramount importance for the understanding of their transport, optical and catalytic properties.

arxiv-2205-06651.title: Univalent typoids
arxiv-2205-06651.creator: Iosif Petrakis
arxiv-2205-06651.description: Abstract A typoid is a type equipped with an equivalence relation, such that the terms of equivalence between the terms of the type satisfy certain conditions, with respect to a given equivalence relation between them, that generalise the properties of the equality terms. The resulting weak 2-groupoid structure can be extended to every finite level.

arxiv-2307-12172.title: Challenges for Monocular 6D Object Pose Estimation in Robotics
arxiv-2307-12172.creator: Stefan Thalhammer, Dominik Bauer, Peter Hönig, Jean-Baptiste Weibel, José García-Rodríguez, Markus Vincze
arxiv-2307-12172.description: Abstract Object pose estimation is a core perception task that enables, for example, object manipulation and scene understanding. The widely available, inexpensive and high-resolution RGB sensors and CNNs that allow for fast inference make monocular approaches especially well suited for robotics applications.

arxiv-2504-16528.title: Quantitative Strategy Templates
arxiv-2504-16528.creator: Ashwani Anand, Satya Prakash Nayak, Ritam Raha, Irmak Sağlam, Anne-Kathrin Schmuck
arxiv-2504-16528.description: Abstract This paper presents (permissive) Quantitative Strategy Templates (QaSTels) to succinctly represent infinitely many winning strategies in two-player energy and mean-payoff games. This transfers the recently introduced concept of Permissive (qualitative) Strategy Templates (PeSTels) for ω \omega -regular games to games with quantitative objectives.

arxiv-2505-08900.title: Generalizable neural-network parameterization of mesoscale eddies in idealized and global ocean models
arxiv-2505-08900.creator: Pavel Perezhogin, Alistair Adcroft, Laure Zanna
arxiv-2505-08900.description: Abstract Data-driven methods have become popular to parameterize the effects of mesoscale eddies in ocean models. However, they perform poorly in generalization tasks and may require retuning if the grid resolution or ocean configuration changes. We address the generalization problem by enforcing physics constraints on a neural network parameterization of mesoscale eddy fluxes.

arxiv-2507-11492.title: Low-redshift analogues of cosmic noon galaxies as laboratories for clumpy star formation
arxiv-2507-11492.creator: Jorge M. Santos-Junior, Thiago S. Gonçalves, Luidhy Santana-Silva, Arianna Cortesi, Karin Menendez-Delmestre, Amanda E. de Araujo-Carvalho
arxiv-2507-11492.description: Abstract It has been established that a significant fraction of star formation at high-redshift occurs in clumpy galaxies. The properties of clumps and their formation mechanisms, however, remain highly debated. In this work we analyse a sample of 18 Supercompact Ultraviolet Luminous Galaxies observed with the OSIRIS spectrograph at the Keck Telescope, targeting their Pa − α -\alpha emission.

pmc-10517468.title: Professional identity formation among undergraduate pre-medical students: a scoping review protocol
pmc-10517468.creator: Meklit Endalcachew, Jennifer Deberg, Melissa Swee, Manish Suneja, Bharat Kumar
pmc-10517468.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). BackgroundProfessional Identity formation is the process by which learners internalize a profession’s values, behaviors, and perceptions. With respect to physicians, this occurs at multiple levels of medical education, including the undergraduate, graduate, and continuing medical education stages. Professional identity formation likely starts even earlier, during the undergraduate pre-medical years but, to date, no known scoping or systematic review has been conducted on this topic.

pmc-10752793.title: 糖尿病肾脏疾病非经典临床类型与病理变化综述
pmc-10752793.creator: Chenxi FANG, Liya SUN, Yan LIU, Li XIAO, Lin SUN
pmc-10752793.description: 糖尿病肾脏疾病（diabetic kidney disease, DKD）是糖尿病的常见并发症，约1/3糖尿病患者可发展至DKD。典型DKD临床早期表现为微量蛋白尿，随着疾病进展可出现大量蛋白尿并伴随肾功能减退。一般认为DKD患者出现大量蛋白尿后病情逆转可能性降低，最终部分患者可发展为终末期肾病（end-stage renal disease, ESRD）。此外，DKD典型病理变化为肾小球基底膜增厚、系膜基质增多、K-W结节及晚期糖尿病肾小球硬化。然而，临床上某些DKD患者，特别是2型糖尿病（type 2 diabetes mellitus, T2DM）合并DKD患者临床表现可呈多样性，疾病进展与转归不同，表现为非经典型DKD类型，如正常白蛋白尿型、蛋白尿缓解型、肾功能快速下降型。此外，肾活检还可见新月体形成这一特殊病理改变。但目前临床医师对此认识尚不足，故值得重视。本文结合国内外文献及本课题组既往研究结果，对非经典DKD临床表型与病理变化进行初步介绍，以期进一步加强临床医生对非经典DKD表型与病理变化的认识，提高我国DKD防治水平。Keywords: 糖尿病肾病, 蛋白尿缓解, 肾功能快速下降, 正常白蛋白尿, 新月体, 综述 中国成人糖尿病 （diabetes mellitus, DM）患病率高达12.4%[1]。大约30%的1型糖尿病患者（type 1 diabetes mellitus, T1DM）和大约40%的2型糖尿病（type 2 diabetes mellitus, T2DM）患者会患上慢性肾脏病（chronic kidney disease, CKD），部分患者甚至可发展至终末期肾病（end stage renal disease, ESRD）[2]。随着DM发病率不断增加，糖尿病肾脏疾病（diabetic kidney disease, DKD）已成为引起ESRD的主要原因[3]。DKD发病机制十分复杂，可能与血流动力学变化、肾小球高滤过、糖脂代谢紊乱、异常炎症因子表达、氧化应激、蛋白激酶C激活、细胞自噬异常等相关[4-7]。目前DKD治疗措施仍然有限，患者常合并不良心血管事件、感染、贫血、营养不良等疾病，死亡风险显著升高[8]，应引起高度重视。 2021年《糖尿病肾脏疾病临床诊疗中国指南》中DKD诊断标准如下：①随机尿白蛋白和肌酐比（urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio, UACR）≥30 mg/g，或尿白蛋白排泄率（urinary albumin excretion rate, UAER）≥30 mg/24 h，3至6个月内复检3次，有2次达到或大于临界值。②估算肾小球滤过率（estimated glomerular filtration rate, eGFR）<60 mL/（min·1.

pmc-11305378.title: Water-powered, electronics-free dressings that electrically stimulate wounds for rapid wound closure
pmc-11305378.creator: Rajaram Kaveti, Margaret A. Jakus, Henry Chen, Bhavya Jain, Darragh G. Kennedy, Elizabeth A. Caso, Navya Mishra, Nivesh Sharma, Baha Erim Uzunoğlu, Won Bae Han, Tae-Min Jang, Suk-Won Hwang, Georgios Theocharidis, Brandon J. Sumpio, Aristidis Veves, Samuel K. Sia, Amay J. Bandodkar
pmc-11305378.description: Chronic wounds affect ~2% of the U.S. population and increase risks of amputation and mortality. Unfortunately, treatments for such wounds are often expensive, complex, and only moderately effective. Electrotherapy represents a cost-effective treatment; however, its reliance on bulky equipment limits its clinical use. Here, we introduce water-powered, electronics-free dressings (WPEDs) that offer a unique solution to this issue.

pmc-11679248.title: Semantically-Enhanced Feature Extraction with CLIP and Transformer Networks for Driver Fatigue Detection
pmc-11679248.creator: Zhen Gao, Xiaowen Chen, Jingning Xu, Rongjie Yu, Heng Zhang, Jinqiu Yang
pmc-11679248.description: Drowsy driving is a leading cause of commercial vehicle traffic crashes. The trend is to train fatigue detection models using deep neural networks on driver video data, but challenges remain in coarse and incomplete high-level feature extraction and network architecture optimization. This paper pioneers the use of the CLIP (Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training) model for fatigue detection.

pmc-12708657.title: Fluid balance and electrolyte losses in collegiate male soccer players in practice and game under different environments
pmc-12708657.creator: Pengwei Ma, Kate Early, Haicheng Li, Guangxia Zhang, Haoyan Wang
pmc-12708657.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The environment poses significant physiologic challenges to athletic performance. The purpose of this study was to investigate fluid balance and electrolyte losses in Chinese collegiate male soccer players during practices and games under different environments. Twelve male players were recruited across 38 practices (P) and 17 games (G) over a 9-month period, conducted in hot (H) and cool (C) environments, yielding four experimental conditions: G + H, P + H, G + C, and P + C.

pmc-12810518.title: Seismic noise in crystal neutron interferometry
pmc-12810518.creator: G. Mana, E. Massa
pmc-12810518.description: A split-crystal neutron interferometer allows longer arm separation and length. However, since the visibility of the interference is sensitive to seismic and acoustic noise, it is crucial to design and operate the interferometer acknowledging this problem. To aid in this process, we present a mathematical model that quantifies how time-dependent accelerations affect the phase and visibility of the interference fringes.

pmc-13197526.title: ‘Fuhui 631’, a novel hybrid rice restorer line with multiple resistance genes, high combining ability, and superior grain quality developed with marker‑assisted breeding
pmc-13197526.creator: Liping Chen, Yongsheng Zhu, Jiahuan Jiang, Linyan Wei, Yingheng Wang, Yanmei Zheng, Qiang Lin, Yanjia Xiao, Yidong Wei, Qiuhua Cai, Fangxi Wu, Huaan Xie, Jianfu Zhang
pmc-13197526.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). released by Rice Research Institute, Fujian Academy of Agricultural Sciences in 2022. It combines high yield potential, strong combining ability, lodging resistance, heat tolerance, and superior grain quality, representing a significant advance over existing restorer lines. Given the increasing challenges of extreme weather and disease pressure in rice production, there is an urgent need for restorer lines that integrate multiple stress resistances with high combining ability and premium grain quality.

pmc-13258575.title: Mechanism Study on the Effects of Yellow River Sediment Silt Powder on Hydration, Microstructure, and Strength Development of Shotcrete
pmc-13258575.creator: Ge Zhang, Xin Wang, Jialing Li, Kunpeng Li, Yuanjian Wang, Ali Raza, Chengfang Yuan
pmc-13258575.description: To investigate the influence mechanism of Yellow River silt powder on the hydration process, microstructure, and strength development of shotcrete, and to promote the resource utilization of Yellow River sediment, this study systematically investigated the effects of different silt powder replacement levels (0%, 10%, 30%, and 50%) on a cement–accelerator system.

pmc-13486826.title: Minimal clinically important difference for cognitive scales in people with Parkinson’s disease with cognitive impairment
pmc-13486826.creator: Ghorban Taghizadeh, Negin Eissazade, Javier Pagonabarraga, Saul Martinez-Horta, Jaime Kulisevsky, Parvaneh Taghavi Azar Sharabiani, Azar Sharabiani, Pouria Akbarikoli, Seyede Zohreh Jazaeri, Maryam Mehdizadeh
pmc-13486826.description: Cognitive impairment (CI) is a significant non-motor symptom of Parkinson’s disease (PD), necessitating effective assessment tools to evaluate treatment efficacy. Minimal Clinically Important Difference (MCID) thresholds provide critical benchmarks for interpreting cognitive intervention outcomes. This study establishes MCID values for PD Cognitive Rating Scale (PD-CRS), Scales for Outcomes in PD-Cognition (SCOPA-COG), and Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) in PD-CI.
